Bruxelles — Brussels, Belgium

In detail

Bruxelles is one of the 19 official communes of the Brussels-Capital Region. BISA (Brussels Institute for Statistics and Analysis), citing Federale Politie figures, recorded 47,888 total registered crimes and misdemeanours here in 2025, across a population of 198,314 residents (Statbel, 2025) — a rate of 24,148 offences per 100,000 residents, roughly 2.0x the citywide commune average. This rate is calculated against registered residents, not footfall, so a busy central, station, or nightlife-heavy commune can read higher without that meaning it is unusually risky to walk through, and a quiet residential commune can show a low rate simply by having few offences relative to its population. The City of Brussels is the region's historic and administrative centre — the Grand-Place/Pentagon, Gare Centrale, Gare du Nord, and a large share of the region's hotels, shops and offices sit here on a comparatively modest resident base, so its rate reflects huge daytime and evening footfall against relatively few registered residents rather than elevated risk per visit. This is Wandroz's official-data layer for Brussels — real BISA / Federale Politie and Statbel figures, not a qualitative or press-based judgment — and the source data is not split here by time of day, so both figures shown here are the same.

Frequently asked questions

Is Bruxelles safe?

Wandroz currently rates Bruxelles in Brussels, Belgium as an area where Wandroz's data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Brussels, Belgium, based on BISA (Brussels Institute for Statistics and Analysis), citing Federale Politie figures. This source has no time-of-day breakdown, so this is one overall level rather than a separately measured day and night figure — see the note on this page before treating the day/night badges as independently measured.

Does Bruxelles's rating cover night-time safety specifically?

Not separately. BISA (Brussels Institute for Statistics and Analysis), citing Federale Politie figures publishes one figure per zone with no time-of-day split, so Bruxelles's day and night badges show the same underlying level rather than an independently measured night figure. Treat it as a general indicator, not a night-specific measurement.

Is Bruxelles a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Bruxelles's rating is a useful general indicator, but this data is normalised against registered residents, not visitor footfall — busy tourist, transit or shopping areas can read higher without that meaning elevated risk for a visitor passing through. What official data is Bruxelles's rating based on?

BISA (Brussels Institute for Statistics and Analysis), citing Federale Politie figures, covering Bruxelles's real administrative boundary.
